assignments.title: Book Data Analysis - Statistical Inference
assignments.description: Analyzed a 52,466-book dataset to identify drivers of pricing and popular demand. Discovered a strong positive correlation ($r \approx 0.709$) between rating count and overall score. ANOVA testing confirmed significant price variance across formats ($F \approx 7.65, p < 10^{-29}$). Highlighted the distinction between $p$-value statistical significance and practical effect size on large-sample correlations ($r \approx 0.026$).

assignments.title: Multilingual Constituency Parsing with Self-Attention and Pre-Training
assignments.description:
A reproduction study of Kitaev et al.’s multilingual constituency parsing approach using self-attention and pre-trained language models. The project evaluated English and Indonesian constituency parsing using English BERT, multilingual BERT (mBERT), and IndoBERT. 
The study implemented and trained a neural chart parser, constructed POS/tag vocabularies, evaluated parsing performance using Precision, Recall, and F1 score, and compared multilingual and language-specific pre-trained models. 
Results showed that English BERT achieved an F1 score of 88.08% on PTB, while mBERT achieved 80.18%. On the Indonesian ICON dataset, IndoBERT achieved 83.40%, outperforming mBERT at 83.13%.
